domains.title: Mountain of the Gods
domains.subtitle: The domain of Ólympos
domains.lead: In the greek location tradition, Ólympos governed mountain of the gods. The name encodes a sphere of power that shaped ritual, narrative, and social order.

cards.title: Primary Sphere
cards.body: Ólympos is principally associated with mountain of the gods.

cards.title: Cultural Role
cards.body: Worshippers approached Ólympos through cult, myth, and the material culture of the greek-location world.

mythology.lead: The myths of Ólympos preserve the name's power and personality across generations of retelling.

myths.title: The story of Ólympos
myths.text: Ólympos appears in greek location tradition as a figure whose domain over mountain of the gods shapes both cosmic order and human experience. The surviving narratives emphasize Ólympos's role, attributes, and relationships with other powers.

lore.syncretism: Greek cult and myth travelled with colonists, traders, and conquerors; Roman adaptation, Hellenistic ruler cult, and later European classicism all recast this name for new audiences.
lore.culturalLegacy: The name endures in place names, scholarly vocabulary, modern fiction, and the ongoing recovery of ancient Greek culture through archaeology and philology. Restoring Ólympos in Unicode preserves the name's cultural specificity against the flattening force of plain ASCII.
lore.extendedMeditation: Names are not merely labels; they are compressed worlds. Ólympos carries within it a greek location understanding of bright, shining mountain. Unicode restoration returns that world to readable form.
sources: Homer. Iliad and Odyssey; Hesiod. Theogony and Works and Days.
Beekes, R. S. P. Etymological Dictionary of Greek. Leiden: Brill, 2010.
Material evidence from the Greek world — inscriptions, sanctuaries, votive deposits, and literary papyri — anchors the name in historical cult.
